subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Plain Bearings: Simple and Silent
description: A micro-lesson that makes Plain Bearings: Simple and Silent usable.

hook.text: Some bearings have no balls or rollers. Just a sleeve and a shaft.

buildup.text: A plain bearing is a smooth bore the shaft slides or floats inside.

discovery.text: With enough oil, the shaft never touches the sleeve — it rides on film.

twist.text: They're quieter and handle shock loads much better than rolling types.

climax.text: Engine crankshaft bearings are plain bearings. They last millions of cycles.

punchline.text: Sometimes the simplest design wins the race.

quiz.question: Why do plain bearings work well for engine crankshafts?
options: They create less noise than ball bearings at high RPM
They absorb shock and run on a continuous oil film
They need no lubrication to function properly
